Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the run chase! The Indian Women make their way out to the middle, followed by Tammy Beaumont and Lauren Winfield. Jhulan Goswami will start with the ball. Mithali Raj is not on the field as she has a sore neck and Harmanpreet Kaur is captaining the side in her absence.

Right then! England Women need 222 runs to win and with the form their batters are in, they should be able to chase it down. India though need to bowl really well if they want to level the series. What will happen? The run chase begins in a while. Do join us then.

India Women were off to a terrific start courtesy Shafali Verma and Smriti Mandhana but they lost three in quick succession to put themselves on the back foot. Mithali Raj and Harmanpreet Kaur did stitch a good partnership but Kaur fell at the wrong time and they lost some wickets quickly. Raj though went on to score another fifty but she fell towards the end and it looked like they will be bowled out below 200 but Goswami and Yadav contributed some vital runs to help India reach 221.

England did not start off too well as Shafali Verma and Smriti Mandhana were off to a good start. But Kate Cross, came on and picked up the wickets of Mandhana and then Rodrigues. Ecclestone picked up Verma soon after and they had India on the mat before the wickets dried up when Mithali Raj and Harmanpreet Kaur were batting. Just then, Cross returned into the attack and picked up three more wickets to end up with a 5-fer. It was the first 5-fer by an English Woman in ODIs since the 2017 World Cup final when Anya Shrubsole took a 6-fer against the same opposition. Katherine Brunt had a tough game while Ecclestone, Sciver and Shrubsole did a decent job.

End of another excellent performance from England Women but they gave away some extra runs towards the end and they might rue that. Overall, it was another good performance in the field and they will be pleased. India Women, on the other hand, would be disappointed and if not for the partnership between Goswami and Yadav, they would have been bowled out below 200.

OUT! STUMPED! Two wickets in quick succession for England! Tossed up delivery around off, Shafali Verma strides forward and is beaten as she looks to play the cut shot. Amy Jones collects the ball and removes the bails in a flash. Verma look to get back in her crease but it does not seem enough. The umpires take it upstairs to check. Amy Jones is very confident that they have got another wicket. The third umpire checks various replays and it seems that Verma has not got back into the crease. Out is the signal. Verma was looking so good but has to depart after a breezy knock.
Commentary.Howout: st Amy Jones b Sophie Ecclestone

On leg, clipped to deep square leg for a single this time.
FOUR! Excellent shot! Length delivery on leg, Smriti Mandhana works it towards deep square leg for a boundary. Elegantly played.
Full and on off, Mandhana pushes it towards mid off for a single.
Fuller on off, Mandhana leans into her shot and drives it towards extra cover.
Outside off, Verma dabs it towards third man for a run.
Fractionally short on middle and leg, Verma guides it to point.
Back of a length delivery on middle, tucked on the leg side.
Short ball on middle, Verma ducks under it.
Short ball on middle, Verma clears her front leg and then pulls it wide of mid on for a single.
On off, pushed to point.
FOUR! This is exceptional batting! Fullish and outside off, Verma hangs back and then drives it through the point region for a boundary.
Short ball on the pads, Mandhana pulls it to fine leg for a single.
Full outside off, pushed to cover.
Short ball on off, Verma pulls it to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Length ball on middle, Verma clips it towards mid-wicket for a single.
FOUR! Beautiful shot! On a length on off, Shafali Verma lofts it over mid off for a boundary.
On middle, played towards mid on.
Length delivery on off, worked towards mid off.
Length delivery outside off, Verma went for the punch but gets beaten.
EDGED BUT SAFE! Short of a length on middle and leg, Mandhana looks to defend but it goes off the outside edge past the slip cordon. A single taken.
WIDE! Way too outside off. Mandhana leaves it alone. Wided.
FOUR! Smacked! Shafali Verma was waiting for this one. Short on middle, Verma whacks it to the deep mid-wicket region for a boundary.
FOUR! This is very well played by Shafali Verma! Short and outside off, Verma clears her front leg and then plays it over the backward point fielder for a boundary.
Short ball on the pads, Mandhana swivels and then pulls it to fine leg for a single.
WIDE! Too high! Short ball around middle, Mandhana ducks under it. Wided.

Good length ball on middle, Mandhana looks to push it on the leg side but misses. Brunt appeals for an LBW. The umpire is not interested. Katherine Brunt walks over to her skipper and they discuss whether to take the review. It seems that Brunt is signalling that it is pitching outside leg and the timer has also finished. The replays show that it was indeed pitching outside leg.
On a length on leg, played towards mid on.
Length delivery on middle, Mandhana tucks it towards mid-wicket.
Back of a length delivery on off, Verma hits it towards covers.
Outside off, Verma plays it towards mid off.
Back of a length delivery on off, Verma is solid in her defense.
Good length delivery on middle, coming in, Verma works it towards mid on.
Length delivery outside off, Verma taps it to point.
On middle, Verma looks to flick but it goes off the pads to short fine leg.
Anya Shrubsole will bowl from the other end with the second new ball.
FOUR! Beautifully played! Back of a length ball on middle, Smriti Mandhana pulls it through mid-wicket and fetches herself a boundary. First boundary of the innings.
Good length delivery on the pads, nipping in, Mandhana looks to work it on the leg side but misses. The ball hits the pads. Brunt appeals for an LBW but the umpire shakes his head.
Length delivery on off, pushed back to the bowler.
Length delivery on leg, Verma whips it to backward square leg for one. She is off the mark as well.
A hint of away swing, outside off, Verma looks to defend off the back foot but gets beaten on the outside edge.
Fuller length on leg, swinging in, Mandhana clips it to deep square leg. She is off the mark with a single.

We are all set to begin the second ODI between England Women and India Women. The England players make their way out to the middle, followed by Smriti Mandhana and Shafali Verma. Katherine Brunt will start with the ball.

India Women (Playing XI) - Smriti Mandhana, Shafali Verma, Jemimah Rodrigues (IN PLACE OF PUNAM RAUT), Mithali Raj (C), Harmanpreet Kaur, Deepti Sharma, Sneh Rana (IN PLACE OF POOJA VASTRAKAR), Taniya Bhatia (WK), Shikha Pandey, Jhulan Goswami, Poonam Yadav (IN PLACE OF EKTA BISHT).

England Women (Unchanged Playing XI) - Lauren Winfield, Tammy Beaumont, Heather Knight (C), Natalie Sciver, Amy Jones (WK), Sophia Dunkley, Katherine Brunt, Sarah Glenn, Sophie Ecclestone, Anya Shrubsole, Kate Cross.
Toss - Up goes the coin and it lands in favour of England. They have elected to field first.

Hello and a warm welcome to the second ODI between India Women and England Women. England are 1-0 ahead in the 3-match series and going by their performance in the first game, it is safe to say that they are the favourites to make it 2-0. India, on the other hand, need to sort out their batting issues if they want to make a comeback. Their bowlers had a tough job to defend and they would hope that their batters do a little better this time around. Toss and team updates in a while.
